shortDescription: Norway has agreed to buy up to 12 million metric tons of carbon credits generated by solar power projects developed by Indonesia's state-owned utility Perusahaan Listrik Negara, the Indonesian government on Thursday.

children: Norway has agreed to buy up to 12 million metric tons of carbon credits generated by solar power projects developed by Indonesia's state-owned utility Perusahaan Listrik Negara, the Indonesian government on Thursday.
The carbon credits are valued at between $20 to $40 per ton of CO2e, the government said in a statement
The deal was signed on the sidelines of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change meeting (COP31) in Turkey
The agreement is expected to provide Indonesia with a sustainable financing mechanism for its energy transition under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement, Jakarta said
This refers to the framework allowing countries to cooperate in reducing emissions through bilateral arrangements
It enables nations with surplus emissions reductions to transfer them in the form of credits to countries seeking to meet their own climate targets
